title: The Assessment of TikTok as a Source of Quality Health Information on Varicoceles
screen_reason: Cross-sectional appraisal of the top 225 TikTok videos for the keyword 'varicocele' (24 May 2022), of which 36 met inclusion criteria and were rated by three urology clinicians. The study's instruments are QUALITY tools - DISCERN and a five-domain completeness score - and those alone would not qualify. But the paper additionally reports an explicit falsity share with a denominator: 23% of videos presented inaccurate information, with named themes (inaccurate causes, symptoms and treatments). That is a CONTENT estimate and makes the paper eligible.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language videos only, searched from a computer in the United States with no TikTok account
estimates.measure_type: % of English-language TikTok videos about varicoceles that presented inaccurate information
estimates.value_raw: 23% of videos (abstract: '23% of videos had misinformation'; Results: 'A substantial portion (23%) of videos presented inaccurate information'). No count is printed and 23% of 36 = 8.3, so the underlying integer is not recoverable.
estimates.denominator: 36 TikTok videos about varicoceles meeting inclusion criteria, screened from the first 225 videos returned by TikTok's 'top' (engagement-ranked) sort for the keyword 'varicocele'; exclusions were off-topic videos tagged with the word, videos not directed at a patient audience, duplicates, and videos narrated or captioned in a language other than English. Creators: 17 general users (47%), 16 healthcare professionals (44%, of whom 2 urologists), 3 scientific communities (8%).
estimates.definition: A video counted if it presented inaccurate information about varicoceles. The paper gives no coding rule, only the themes found: "inaccurate varicocele causes (ie, 'pooling of toxic blood'), symptoms (ie, 'clear and watery semen'), and treatment options (ie, herbal remedies)", set against listed examples of correct content (dilation of the pampiniform plexus, incompetent valves, impaired sperm production, observation, surgical ligation, embolization).
estimates.misinfo_def: No definition is offered. The operative phrase is "A substantial portion (23%) of videos presented inaccurate information", with accuracy judged against the clinical knowledge of the three urology raters.
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 172 (end of the DISCERN paragraph); restated in the Abstract ('23% of videos had misinformation') and the Discussion ('nearly one-quarter of videos presented misinformation')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Three clinicians - a pediatric urology attending, a urology resident and a pediatric urology nurse practitioner - independently rated every video. Fleiss' kappa was 0.812 ('almost perfect') but is reported specifically for 'the quality of the videos', i.e. the DISCERN and completeness ratings; the paper never states who made the accuracy/inaccuracy determination, whether it was made independently by all three, or how disagreement was resolved. The 0.812 therefore should NOT be read as reliability for this row's numerator.
estimates.moderator_quote: Using the key word "varicocele," the first 225 videos delivered by TikTok's "top" sorting process on May 24, 2022 were retrieved. This sorting is based on the highest TikTok user engagement. A search was performed on the web-based application using a computer that had never been previously used to access TikTok and the search was done without logging into a personal TikTok account.
estimates.notes: Confidence medium, on three grounds. (a) The percentage does not reduce to a whole number of videos: 23% of 36 is 8.3, and neither 8/36 (22.2%) nor 9/36 (25%) rounds to 23%; the count is nowhere printed, so either the denominator for this particular figure differs from 36 or the percentage is loosely rounded. I have kept the verbatim 23% against the paper's only stated denominator and flagged the mismatch rather than reverse-engineering a count. (b) The misinformation determination has no documented procedure, unlike the DISCERN and completeness ratings which are fully specified - it surfaces in a single sentence at the end of a results paragraph. (c) n = 36 is very small, so the 95% interval around 23% is roughly 11-39%. Structural notes: the corpus is rank-truncated to TikTok's engagement-ranked 'top' 225 and then heavily filtered (225 to 36, an 84% attrition), hence denom_selection=curated; the search was deliberately de-personalised (fresh device, no login) which is good practice against algorithmic tailoring. breadth coded 'false' because two of the three example themes are plain factual errors about causes and symptoms; the third (herbal remedies) is unproven rather than false, which nudges toward 'misleading' - a defensible alternative. population_scope=general_public reflects an open-platform corpus, though the creator mix is nearly half clinicians. The Results sentence ('A substantial portion (23%) of videos presented inaccurate information') sits in a two-column layout and is not quotable as a contiguous span, so the source_quote is the abstract's statement of the same figure.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, deliberately: (1) The DISCERN scores (22.2 +/- 13.1 for healthcare professionals vs 16.1 +/- 4.7 for non-healthcare, p < .05; verbal ratings 'poor' and 'very poor'). DISCERN is named in the protocol as a QUALITY instrument, and decisively these are reported only as means of a scale, not as a share of videos - so no row. (2) The entire completeness matrix in Table 2 (e.g. healthcare professionals: definition 62.5% no content / 12.5% some / 25% extensive; symptoms 50% / 43.75% / 6.25%; evaluation 93.75% no content; outcomes 100% no content; non-healthcare: definition 88% no content, evaluation 100% no content). These are the clearest QUALITY-not-CONTENT figures in the paper: a wholly TRUE video that simply does not mention evaluation scores 'no content', so the label attaches to accurate material and cannot be a falsity share. The protocol's completeness rule sends these to QUALITY, and since they are shares rather than means one could argue for keeping them as QUALITY rows; I have not, because they measure omission across five separate domains and would generate ten rows carrying no veracity information at all, against R4. (3) Engagement figures (2,626,560 total views, 189,262 likes, 2,393 comments; median views 3,867 vs 3,500, p = .05; likes 172 vs 82, p = .07) - no share of exposure or sharing attributable to misinformation is reported, so no EXPOSURE or SHARING row is possible; in particular the paper never crosses engagement with the accuracy judgement, so the 23% cannot be weighted by views. (4) Creator composition (17 general users 47%, 16 healthcare professionals 44%, 3 scientific communities 8%, 2 urologists) - source structure, not veracity, and no top-group share of activity is given, so R1 rules out any CONCENTRATION row. (5) 'Only 22% of videos contained information that can also be found in the EAU guidelines' from O'Sullivan et al., 'Ninety-six percent of parents are using social media as a source of pediatric health information', and 'at least 15% of adolescent boys' have varicoceles - all figures cited from other sources, barred by R8. Unresolved: whether the 23% was applied to all 36 included videos or to some subset (see the arithmetic note in the row).

rob.design: Single-timepoint cross-sectional content appraisal. Sampling frame: the first 225 videos returned by TikTok's engagement-based 'top' sort for the single keyword 'varicocele' on 24 May 2022, retrieved via the web application on a device that had never accessed TikTok and without logging in - a deliberate and effective control for algorithmic personalisation, but one that fixes the corpus to a single query, a single day and a single ranking regime. Screening to 36 videos (Fig. 1) removed off-topic, non-patient-directed, duplicate and non-English videos, an 84% attrition that is described but not enumerated step by step. Rating: three clinicians (pediatric urology attending, urology resident, pediatric urology nurse practitioner) independently scored every video on a five-domain 0-2 completeness scale and on the 15-item DISCERN instrument, with scores averaged across raters; Fleiss' kappa 0.812 for video quality. The accuracy judgement that yields this review's estimate is reported without a stated procedure, rater set, or reliability figure. No sample-size justification, no sensitivity analysis, no protocol registration mentioned; no limitations section. n = 36 is small and English-only, so the estimate is imprecise and its population of content is one keyword's worth of an English-language TikTok ranking.
rob.item6_quote: Themes of misinformation included inaccurate varicocele causes (ie, "pooling of toxic blood"), symptoms (ie, "clear and watery semen"), and treatment options (ie, herbal remedies).
rob.item10_quote: Thirty-six videos met inclusion criteria. ... A substantial portion (23%) of videos presented inaccurate information.
